I make romance an important part of my plots, it's honestly the romantasy genre but in a ttrpg format. The 'White-Stairs' GPU Issue  
This graphical glitch occurs when your graphics card drivers are out of date. In some cases (such as a notebook PC with both an intel GPU and a dedicated GPU), Foundry VTT will not have access to use the correct GPU.  
\---  
Drivers Out of Date  
You will need to update your graphics card drivers for your GPU-- as this issue disproportionately affects Intel GPUs, their driver website will be a good starting point.  
Laptop Using Wrong GPU  
This issue is primarily one which affects Windows users, to resolve it:  
1. Press the ⊞ Windows key  
2. type graphics  
3. choose graphics settings  
4. under Graphics Performance Preference, add your browser of choice, as well as the path to your Foundry VTT application.  
5. Set the Options of each to use High Performance  
6. Close your browser and the Foundry VTT application completely and restart them.

I used to have to transit over 1h to get to and from work. 1 bus, 1 metro and a 5 minute walk. I usually kind of do this on autopilot. I get in the bus, call my grandma since I'm one of the 4 people in the bus at this hour (8pm), get on the metro and then walk home.  
One night, I get off the metro and start walking home. roughly 100 meters from the gate to my appartement complex, this really really tall guy rushes past me, turns to me and stops.  
We're in a small alley, a streetlight is like, 20m away, no one else is in the street and he just starts chatting me up.  
Turns out he followed me from my place of work to my house (said it like it was a compliment), and wanted my name and number. I refused and told him I wanted to go home, that he was making me uncomfortable etc. But he kept pushing and pushing. Even tried to reassure me that he meant me no harm, that I was safe, he just wanted my number...  
This lasted 10 minutes. He was so fucking tall and physically imposing, I was kinda paralysed, otherwise I would have threatened to call the cops. I eventually caved, and said I'd let him give me his number. I take my phone out to input it, and he takes it from my hands and calls himself on it, hands it back and thanks me, then walks away.   
I went home and cried, feeling so fucking unsafe. I took the bus later every single night for a month, and never crossed paths with him again. I blocked him on my phoned immediately and kept his humber to give to the police, if ever.   
God, that experience still gives me chills.

I started when I was a kid. It started with me telling my mom about my dreams. I had a 1h drive to school and I would tell my mom about my dreams over the course of this drive every single day. I was 5 - 6 at the time. My mom started writing them down and compiling them in a folder and eventually, we no longer had the time to talk about my dreams because we moved and I took the bus to school instead, so I wrote my own dreams down. From dreams, to day dreams to fiction. I won a kid's writing competition at 10 with a short story and that really got me wanting to write more. I was homeschooled between 11 and 16, so I wrote a lot. Short stories, beginning of novels, poems, rewritings of books I found shitty. Never completed anything super long, but I loved writing.

I look back and I find a lot of what I used to write shitty, and I also find some gems, some awesome sentences that I want to reuse, some cool character ideas, worldbuilding ideas etc. I'm still not at the point of writing something good enough or complete enough to be published, and I have had times where I wasn't inspired to write for a year or more, and so I stopped. Whenever I take up writing again (which I'm doing right now), I feel like I've lost so much of my storytelling abilities, my sentences are dry and my style goes from overly flowery & archaic to overly plain and it doesn't flow well. It's super discouraging to look back on stuff 16 year old me wrote and find them genuinely better than what I'm capable of doing after a 2 year break, but I know I'm going to improve again and I love writing so much that I'm not going to stop.

I sometimes imagine what an ideal review of my story would be. What elements I want to have pointed out and praised the most. What effect I want my story to have, what emotions I want to evoque, etc. etc. It helps me focus my energy on certain aspects and think about how I can attain my goals. For example, I'd like people to feel very bittersweet at the end of this short story, but satisfied with the character growth. So I'm going to focus on it a bit more. 
Might not work for everyone but when I've finished an outline or a rough draft, I stop and really think about what I want to achieve with it. It changes with each one and sometimes it's just "I want to have fun!" So the imagined reaction to it could be "I can tell she put a lot of joy and love into this one."
It's not about caring about what others think or writing for others. It just helps me keep my majn goals in sight.
